gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: My brother is six foot three — he is much ___ than me.
gaps.explanation: 'Tall' is used for people's height, so the comparative is 'taller'; 'higher' is for heights above a level.

gaps.sentence: She has had a brilliant ___ in politics.
gaps.hint: the whole course of a person's professional life
gaps.explanation: 'Career' is the progress through a working life, especially in one profession; 'job' is one position.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: The factory ___ waste into the river for years before being fined.
gaps.explanation: 'Discharge waste' = release it into the environment.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.

gaps.sentence: After dinner we had chocolate cake for ___.
gaps.hint: the sweet course of a meal (double 's' like 'sweet stuff')
gaps.explanation: 'Dessert' is the sweet course at the end of a meal; 'desert' is a dry, sandy region.

gaps.sentence: Please be ___ — the baby is sleeping.
gaps.explanation: 'Quiet' means making little or no noise; 'quite' is an adverb meaning fairly or completely.
